newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends down in thin deals.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends down in thin deals.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - The market ended down after drifting in tight ranges on lack of participation ahead of KLCE dinner this weekend. Trading volume fell sharply with players also sidelined because of lack of fresh news. Dec futures traded in four-ringgit range, will move between 1,140 and 1,180.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Prices drifted, with players awaiting Ivan Wong report and PORLA data next week.

Traders also attributed the quietness to players' unwillingness to trade ahead of a private forecaster, Ivan Wong report and key Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) September crop data next week.
Earlier, sentiment eased on spill-over selling from Thursday's close after news that Pakistan was seeking a smaller loan than anticipated, traders said.

The state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan said on Thursday it was negotiating for a $5 million financing facility with the Islamic Development Bank to import vegetable oils, quashing earlier talk that Pakistan has secured a $10 million.
By the close of day, December futures contract eased seven ringgit to 1,157 ringgit ($461.69) a tonne.
The market is expected to ease slightly and consolidate around current levels.

Physicals saw dealings in October (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,175 ringgit a tonne with bids at 1,170. Oct (central) was offered at 1,160 and bids at 1,150, and Oct (north) at 1,145 against 1,130.
